walkthroughs.body_html:
After the first months of fighting in 1914, both sides 'dug in'.

The Western Front became a line of trenches over 400 miles long, from the Belgian coast to the Swiss border.

Between the two armies lay No Man's Land, criss-crossed with barbed wire and shell holes. 🌧️

A trench had a fire step to stand on, dugouts to sleep in, and zig-zags to limit blast damage.

Daily routine: 'stand-to' at dawn, repairs, sentry duty, sleep, food, letters home. Rats stole rations; lice lived in uniforms.

In cold mud feet rotted — called trench foot. Endless shelling left many soldiers with shell shock.

To attack, soldiers had to climb out and run across No Man's Land — 'going over the top'.

They faced machine guns, barbed wire and artillery. Gains were tiny — sometimes a field, for thousands of lives.

On the first day of the Somme (1 July 1916), Britain lost about 57,000 men in a single day. Soldiers wrote bitter poems about what they saw. 📝

mcqs.q: Did Gorbachev intend to dissolve the Soviet Union?
options: Jews were expelled because they refused to fight in the Crusades.
No — he wanted to reform and save Soviet socialism; glasnost and perestroika unleashed forces (nationalism, economic chaos) he could not control.
Gorbachev took power planning to abolish communism and dissolve the USSR.
Gorbachev dissolved the USSR by signing a treaty with Ronald Reagan.

mcqs.q: Was the English Civil War caused by religion alone?
options: Jews were expelled because they refused to fight in the Crusades.
The Civil War was a war of religion between Catholics and Protestants.
No — religion (Laudian reforms, Scottish Presbyterians) combined with financial disputes (ship money), political conflict over parliamentary rights, and Charles I's personal style.
The Civil War began because Cromwell wanted to be king.

mcqs.q: Why were Jews expelled from England in 1290?
options: Edward I expelled Jews after a century of restrictions and taxation had impoverished the community; antisemitism, debts owed to Jews, and political pressure all contributed.
Jews left England voluntarily because they were no longer welcome.
